title: Ruling 2023-01: Pump Truck Operated by Concrete Retailer is Nontaxable Service
text:
Date: July 6, 2023

Written by: Emily Bergquist

Approved by: Craig Bolio, Commissioner of Taxes

This is a formal ruling for your company, [Taxpayer], (Taxpayer), regarding the applicability of sales tax to sales of concrete, delivery charges and charges for use of Taxpayer’s pump truck. This ruling is based upon representations in your letter dated [date], received in this office [date], the letter of [individual], dated [date], and telephone conversations with [individual].

Ruling 

Based upon the facts presented, charges for your concrete pump truck are not subject to sales tax.

Facts 

Taxpayer is a Vermont business that [deleted]. Taxpayer’s customers are contractors who use the concrete to improve the real property of the contractor or the contractor’s customer.

When a customer has contracted for a purchase of concrete, Taxpayer delivers the concrete to the customer’s site in one of its mixer trucks.

A mixer truck has a rotating drum that mixes the concrete during transportation. Constant mixing of the concrete is necessary to prevent the concrete from setting before it is delivered.

Once at the customer’s site, the mixer truck discharges the concrete directly from the truck’s mixer drum onto the desired location, directing the flow by means of a chute or trough or slide attached to the mixer truck.

For smaller amounts of concrete, the customer may then convey the concrete from the delivery site by wheelbarrow to the forms being used to place the concrete.

In some cases, the mixer truck may discharge concrete into a large bucket which is then lifted by a crane to higher elevations or over obstacles, where the crane operator controls the pouring of concrete from the bucket to place the concrete.

In cases where concrete must be moved from the delivery site a greater distance, the mixer truck may discharge its concrete onto a conveyor belt or platform, which moves the concrete over the longer horizontal or vertical distance to where the concrete is to be placed.

In addition to its mixer trucks, Taxpayer operates concrete pump trucks which a customer may request for use in placing the concrete in the desired area of the customer’s building site. The mixer truck in that case will transport the concrete to the customer’s construction site and there discharge the concrete into the pump truck operated by Taxpayer’s employee. A pump truck is not used for transport of concrete to the customer’s job site, and use of the pump truck is completely optional. Once concrete is discharged from the mixer truck into the pump truck, the pump truck pumps the concrete horizontally or vertically through a hose, to place the concrete as required. A customer may request a pump truck because it saves the customer the labor costs of manual placing concrete and ensures accurate measurement of the amount of concrete to be placed in forms at the construction site. The customer is charged separately for the pump truck and its operation.

You have asked whether Taxpayer must collect sales tax on the charge for the pump truck to place the concrete at the customer’s construction site.

Discussion 

Vermont sales tax is imposed at the rate of six percent (1) on the “sales price” of a “retail sale” of “tangible personal property” in Vermont. 32 V.S.A. § 9771.

Taxpayer’s customers are contractors who use the concrete to improve the real property of the contractor or contractor’s customers. A taxable “retail sale” includes a sale to a contractor for use in improving real property. 32 V.S.A. §9701(5). Taxpayer must therefore collect sales tax on its sales of concrete to contractors.

The “sales price” includes “delivery charges” and “charges by the seller for any services necessary to complete the sale, other than installation charges.” 32 V.S.A. § 9701(4)(A)(iii), (iv).

“Delivery charges” are for “delivery to a location designated by the purchaser . . . including, but not limited to, transportation, shipping, postage, handling, crating, and packing.” Vermont Department of Taxes Sales and Use Tax Regulations (Effective date: January 1, 2019) (“Reg.”) § 1.9701(4)-1. “If the seller elects not to allocate the delivery charge, the entire charge is subject to the tax.” Id. Here, Taxpayer charges the customer a single sales price for the concrete and delivery of the concrete in its mixer truck. That single sales price is subject to sales tax.

Once at the site, the mixer truck discharges the concrete at the area “designated by the purchaser.” The customer directs where the concrete must be discharged; for example, onto the ground, into a wheelbarrow, into a crane bucket, or into a waiting pump truck, whether that pump truck is the customer’s or is Taxpayer’s pump truck requested by the customer. The discharge completes delivery of the concrete.

Use of Taxpayer’s pump truck is a separate transaction from the sale and delivery of the concrete. A pump truck is never used to transport (deliver) concrete to the job site. Rental of Taxpayer’s pump truck and operator is completely optional; it is not a “service necessary to complete the sale” of the concrete. The pump truck is machinery used to place concrete after the concrete has been delivered to the job site. The charge for the pump truck and operator is therefore not included as a “delivery charge” in the taxable “sales price” of the concrete.

Nor is rental of Taxpayer’s pump truck and operator itself a taxable transaction. A taxable “lease or rental” is “any transfer of possession or control of the tangible personal property.” Reg. § 1.9701(5)-2. Taxpayer does not transfer possession or control of the pump truck to its customer; Taxpayer retains possession and control of the truck at all times, so this is not a taxable lease or rental. And specifically, a taxable “lease or rental” excludes “providing tangible personal property along with an operator for a fixed or indeterminate period of time [where] the operator is necessary for the equipment to perform as designed.” Reg. § 1.9701(5)-2.A.3.

As a result, the separate charge for the pump truck is not subject to sales tax.

General Provisions 

Issuance of this ruling is conditioned upon the understanding that neither the taxpayer nor a related taxpayer is currently under audit or involved in an administrative appeal or litigation concerning the subject matters of the ruling. This ruling is issued solely to the taxpayer and is limited to the facts presented, as affected by current statutes and regulations.

Other taxpayers may refer to this ruling, when redacted to protect confidentiality, to see the Department's general approach, but the Department will not be bound by this ruling in the case of any other taxpayer or in the case of any change in the relevant statutes or regulations.

This ruling will be made public after deletion of the taxpayer’s name and any information which may identify the taxpayer. A copy of this ruling showing the proposed deletions is attached, and you may request within 30 days that the Commissioner delete any further information that might identify the taxpayer. The final discretion as to deletions rests with the Commissioner.

You have the right to appeal this ruling within 30 days. 3 V.S.A. §§ 808, 815.

1 An additional one-percent sales tax will also apply to taxable sales in any Vermont municipality which has adopted a local option sales tax as provided in 24 V.S.A. § 138.
